evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. praesum: to have the charge or command of

terms.grammar: with the dative, or in Tacitus the accusative
evidence: Tac. Ann. 12.29: quī Pannoniam praesidēbat, who commanded in Pannonia (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To guard, to preside over; of commanding, Lewis & Short cites Tacitus, with the accusative (exercitum, Ann. 3.39) as well as the dative.

evidence: Cic. Leg. 3.2.5 (Lewis & Short: “in publicists’ and milit. lang., to command, govern, rule over”)

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 178, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
